Oral medicine (MFDS 201802575)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201802575. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is used for the relief of the various symptoms of colds (runny nose, nasal congestion, sneezing, sore throat, chills (feeling cold and shivering), fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for the relief of the various symptoms of colds (runny nose, nasal congestion, sneezing, sore thro

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201802575. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

People aged 15 years and older and adults take 2 tablets as 1 dose, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious and potentially fatal skin reactions such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, and toxic epidermal necrolysis have been reported; if a skin rash or other signs of a hypersensitivity reaction appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.
  • If a severe skin adverse reaction such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, those who have experienced asthma when taking other antipyretic analgesics or cold remedies, infants (nursing infants, newborns) under 3 months of age, and patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption must not take this medicine.Before taking this medicine, infants (nursing infants, newborns) infected with or suspected of having chickenpox or influenza and children under 15 years of age, children under 2 years of age, those with an allergic constitution, those who have experienced allergic reactions (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.), people with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, edema (swelling), gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision, etc.), or difficulty urinating (passing urine), elderly people, physically weak people or people with a high fever, people with heartburn, gastric discomfort, stomach pain, ulcer, or bleeding problems, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women, and patients who smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough persisting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever and rash or persistent headache should consult a doctor or pharmacist.Strictly observe the specified dosage and administration.Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.If there is no improvement in symptoms after taking it about 5 to 6 times, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness (congested and reddened skin), itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema (swelling), difficulty urinating (passing urine), thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, rarely shock symptoms (urticaria, edema (swelling), or chest tightness immediately after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, difficulty breathing, etc.), mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome) (accompanied by high fever, with severe symptoms such as rash and redness (congested and reddened skin) and burn-like blistering appearing on the skin over the whole body, the mouth, or the mucous membranes of the eyes), asthma, liver function disorder (generalized lassitude, jaundice (the skin or the whites of the eyes turn yellow), etc.), interstitial pneumonia (accompanied by cough, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, fever, etc.), weakness, cramps in the limbs, or paralysis occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.), antitussives (which stop coughing) and expectorants (phlegm remedies), other cold remedies, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis (nasal inflammation), motion sickness remedies, anti-allergy remedies).
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with diabetes medicines, gout medicines, arthritis medicines, anticoagulants, steroids, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol, potassium-containing preparations, licorice-containing preparations, preparations containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, loop diuretics (furosemide, etacrynic acid), or thiazide diuretics (trichlormethiazide).
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

This medicine is used for cough, phlegm, and hoarseness of the throat, pain and swelling of the throat, and throat discomfort caused by inflammation of the throat.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for cough, phlegm, and hoarseness of the throat, pain and swelling of the throat, and throat disco

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 200101057. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Adults and adolescents aged 15 years and older take 1 sachet as 1 dose, those aged 11 years or older and under 15 years take 2/3 of a sachet as 1 dose, those aged 7 years or older and under 11 years take 1/2 of a sachet as 1 dose, and those aged 3 years or older and under 7 years take 1/3 of a sachet as 1 dose, 3 to 6 times a day without water. The interval between doses should be 2 hours or more.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant, people who are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian drugs, etc.) or who stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks, children under 3 years of age, and patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take this medicine (applies to the mint flavor).
  • Before taking this medicine, people with an allergic constitution, people who have experienced allergic symptoms from medicines (e.g., fever, rash, joint pain, itching, etc.), patients with diseases such as liver disease, kidney disease, thyroid disease, or diabetes, patients with a high fever, frail people, patients with heart disease and high blood pressure, elderly people, breastfeeding women, patients with edema (swelling), patients with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, or emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts 1 week or more or recurs, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash, or persistent headache, and people who have experienced hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to Yellow No. 5 (applies to the mint flavor and the mint coffee flavor) should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration exactly.
  • When giving it to a child, administer it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Possible side effects

  • If rash, redness (congested and reddened skin), itching, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, dizziness, decreased urine volume, swelling of the face and limbs, heaviness of the eyelids, stiffening of the hands, increased blood pressure, headache, weakness, cramps in the limbs, or paralysis occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take together with other antitussives and expectorants, cold remedies, antihistamines, sedatives, or alcohol.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you use it together with potassium-containing preparations, licorice-containing preparations, preparations containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, loop diuretics (furosemide, etacrynic acid), or thiazide diuretics (trichlormethiazide).
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

Oral medicine (MFDS 202401275)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202401275. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is used to relieve various symptoms of a cold, such as runny nose, nasal congestion, sneezing, sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills, fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used to relieve various symptoms of a cold, such as runny nose, nasal congestion, sneezing, sore throat

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202401275. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

People aged 15 years and over take 2 sachets per dose, children aged 11 years to under 15 years take 4/3 sachet per dose, children aged 7 years to under 11 years take 1 sachet per dose, children aged 3 years to under 7 years take 2/3 sachet per dose, and children aged 2 years to under 3 years take 1/2 sachet per dose, 3 times a day 30 minutes after a meal and, if necessary, at bedtime. Leave an interval of 4 hours between doses.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), have been reported, and if a skin rash or another sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily amount of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be taken by patients who have or have had hypersensitivity to this medicine, by people who have had an asthma attack after taking this medicine or its components, another antipyretic analgesic or a cold remedy, or by infants under 3 months of age and children under 2 years of age.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is a child under 2 years of age for whom it is strictly necessary, is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has or is suspected of having chickenpox or influenza, has an allergic constitution, is a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant or a breast-feeding woman, has experienced allergic symptoms caused by a medicine such as fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching, is elderly, is physically weak or has a high fever, or has or has had hypersensitivity to the caramel component.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user has a liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma or difficulty urinating, has persistent or recurrent stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or a bleeding problem, smokes, has asthma, chronic bronchitis or emphysema, or has a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts for 1 week or more or recurs, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash or persistent headache.
  • If the symptoms do not get better after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Children should take it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Do not take it continuously for a long period.
  • Drowsiness may occur while taking it.
  • Avoid driving a car or operating machinery.
  • Follow the prescribed directions and amounts.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema, dizziness, anxiety, tremor or insomnia appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If shock (anaphylaxis), in which urticaria, swelling and a feeling of tightness in the chest appear right after taking it together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing, or mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), asthma, generalized languor, hepatic impairment such as jaundice, or interstitial pneumonia rarely appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • While taking this medicine, do not take antitussives and expectorants, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives or oral medicines containing an antihistamine.
  • People who are taking an MAO inhibitor used for the treatment of depression, Parkinson's disease and the like, or who are within 2 weeks of stopping one, should not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, people who are being given a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant, a steroid or the like should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Patients who are being given a barbiturate, a tricyclic antidepressant or alcohol should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

This drug is used for the relief of pain related to the esophagus, stomach, and duodenum in adults, acute and chronic diarrhea in adults, and acute diarrhea in children aged 24 months or older.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This drug is used for the relief of pain related to the esophagus, stomach, and duodenum in adults, acute and chronic di

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 200201403. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Adults take 3 g as 1 dose, 3 times a day. During the first 3 days of acute diarrhea, the daily dose may be doubled (2 times). For esophagitis, take it after meals; for other indications, take it between meals. Children aged 24 months and older take 6 to 9 g a day divided into 3 doses for 3 days, and then 6 g a day divided into 3 doses for the following 4 days. Shake the suspension well before taking it.

Precautions for use

  • Children under 24 months of age, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant, and breastfeeding women must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, patients with severe chronic constipation, and those who have experienced intestinal obstruction (blocked bowel) should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • When giving this medicine to children, administer it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • If dehydration occurs, provide appropriate fluid replacement.

Possible side effects

  • If abdominal distension, vomiting, constipation, urticaria, rash, itching, and angioedema occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Because the drug has adsorptive properties and may affect the absorption rate or absorption time when taken together with other drugs, it is advisable to take it at an interval.

This medicine is used for supplying vitamins B2 and B6 when physical strength is reduced by physical fatigue, pregnancy and breastfeeding, or illness (while ill or after recovery); for the relief of angular cheilitis (inflammation of the corners of the mouth), cheilitis (inflammation of the lips), stomatitis (inflammation of the mouth), glossitis (inflammation of the tongue), eczema, and dermatitis; and for muscle cramps caused by magnesium deficiency.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for supplying vitamins B2 and B6 when physical strength is reduced by physical fatigue, pregnancy

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202204434. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Those aged 12 years and over and adults take 20 mL at a time, twice a day, between meals (between one meal and the next).

Precautions for use

  • Patients hypersensitive to this medicine, nursing infants under 12 months of age, and patients with severe renal (kidney) failure must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, nursing infants under 1 year of age, pregnant women and women who may be pregnant, breastfeeding women, premature infants, young children, patients with cardiac or circulatory dysfunction, renal (kidney) disorder or hypoproteinemia, and those who have experienced hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to caramel should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • When giving it to a child, administer it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • It may turn the urine yellow and thereby affect clinical test values.

Possible side effects

  • If red spots, diarrhea, asystole (cessation of the heartbeat), or reduced central nervous system function occurs, or if there is no improvement in symptoms after about 1 month of taking it, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral (taken by mouth) tetracycline preparations, antacids, or levodopa.
  • Take care, because taking it together with antialdosterone agents or triamterene may cause hyperkalemia.
  • Avoid teas containing tannin such as green tea and black tea while taking it and just before and after taking it.

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported; if a skin rash or another sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take this medicine together with other products containing acetaminophen.

Precautions for use

  • Patients who are hypersensitive to this medicine, patients with peptic ulcer, severe blood abnormalities, liver disorder, kidney disorder or reduced heart function, and patients with aspirin-induced asthma (asthma attacks triggered by non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs) or who have experienced it must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, patients with liver disorder, kidney disorder, peptic ulcer or blood abnormalities or who have experienced these, patients with a tendency to bleed, abnormal heart function, hypersensitivity or bronchial asthma, the elderly, children under 2 years of age, and pregnant or breastfeeding women should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms (difficulty breathing, reddening of the whole body, angioedema, urticaria, etc.), asthma attack, thrombocytopenia, granulocytopenia, hemolytic (red-blood-cell-destroying) anemia, methemoglobinemia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), cyanosis, hypersensitivity symptoms (facial swelling, difficulty breathing, sweating, low blood pressure, shock), nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, gastrointestinal abnormalities such as gastrointestinal bleeding, peptic ulcer or perforation, rash, allergic reaction, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), high anion gap metabolic acidosis, elevated AST or elevated ALT occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Patients who have taken barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol, and those taking this medicine together with warfarin, lithium, thiazide diuretics or flucloxacillin, should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

People aged 15 years and over take 2 sachets per dose, children aged 11 years to under 15 years take 4/3 sachet per dose, children aged 7 years to under 11 years take 1 sachet per dose, children aged 3 years to under 7 years take 2/3 sachet per dose, and children aged 2 years to under 3 years take 1/2 sachet per dose, 3 times a day 30 minutes after a meal and, if necessary, at bedtime.   • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.

  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), have been reported, and if a skin rash or another sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

  • Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be taken by patients who have or have had hypersensitivity to this medicine, by people who have had an asthma attack after taking this medicine or its components, another antipyretic analgesic or a cold remedy, or by infants under 3 months of age and children under 2 years of age.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is a child under 2 years of age for whom it is strictly necessary, is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has or is suspected of having chickenpox or influenza, has an allergic constitution, is a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant or a breast-feeding woman, has experienced allergic symptoms caused by a medicine such as fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching, is elderly, is physically weak or has a high fever, or has or has had hypersensitivity to the caramel component.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user has a liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma or difficulty urinating, has persistent or recurrent stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or a bleeding problem, smokes, has asthma, chronic bronchitis or emphysema, or has a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts for 1 week or more or recurs, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash or persistent headache.
  • If the symptoms do not get better after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Children should take it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Do not take it continuously for a long period.
  • Drowsiness may occur while taking it.
  • Avoid driving a car or operating machinery.
  • Follow the prescribed directions and amounts.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema, dizziness, anxiety, tremor or insomnia appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • While taking this medicine, do not take antitussives and expectorants, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives or oral medicines containing an antihistamine.
  • People who are taking an MAO inhibitor used for the treatment of depression, Parkinson's disease and the like, or who are within 2 weeks of stopping one, should not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, people who are being given a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant, a steroid or the like should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Patients who are being given a barbiturate, a tricyclic antidepressant or alcohol should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

At a glance

Category

How it works

This medicine is used as an adjunct in the treatment of chronic polyarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, arthropathy, ankylo

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201702324. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Adults take 1 capsule (300 mg) at a time, 2 to 4 times a day. However, do not exceed 4 capsules (1,200 mg) a day.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious, potentially fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction, and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration, and perforation may occur.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, patients with or a history of gastrointestinal ulcer, patients with bleeding in the gastrointestinal tract, the cerebral blood vessels, or other sites, severe blood disorders, severe liver disorder, severe kidney disorder, severe cardiac insufficiency, severe high blood pressure, or bronchial asthma or a history of it, those who have experienced asthma, urticaria, or an allergic reaction to aspirin or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, patients being treated for pain before or after coronary artery (heart artery) bypass graft surgery (CABG), pregnant women at 6 months of pregnancy or later, nursing mothers, patients with inflammatory bowel disease such as Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis, and those who have experienced gastrointestinal bleeding or perforation from previous treatment with non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, patients with or a history of blood disorders, patients with a bleeding tendency, patients with or a history of liver disorder or kidney disorder, patients with fluid retention (accumulation of body fluid) or heart failure, patients with high blood pressure, those who have experienced hypersensitivity, patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) or mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD), elderly people, children aged 6 years and older, patients with stomach cancer or alcoholism, pregnant women in early or mid pregnancy and women who may be pregnant, patients with ischemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease, cerebrovascular disease, or risk factors for cardiovascular disease (e.g., high blood pressure, hyperlipidemia, diabetes, smoking), patients with hepatic porphyria, patients who have had major surgery that caused blood loss, patients with a blood coagulation disorder or who are receiving anticoagulants, and those who have experienced hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to Yellow No. 5 should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Considering the importance of the drug treatment, either stop breastfeeding or stop taking the drug.
  • Dizziness or fatigue may occur after taking this medicine, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.
  • When it is taken for a long period for an acute illness, in principle this should be limited to within 5 days.

Possible side effects

  • If the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist: rarely shock (chest discomfort, chills, difficulty breathing, lowered blood pressure, etc.); rarely blood disorders such as aplastic anemia, hemolytic anemia, granulocytopenia, leukopenia, agranulocytosis, pancytopenia, thrombocytopenia, decreased platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), and eosinophilia; indigestion, abdominal distension, heartburn, upper abdominal pain, diarrhea or constipation; occasionally loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, or stomach discomfort; rarely esophagitis, esophageal stricture, worsening of diverticula, nonspecific hemorrhagic colitis, ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease, peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, bloody stools, gastritis, or pancreatitis; very rarely thirst, stomatitis, erythema multiforme, systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), or hair loss; occasionally angioedema; rarely Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome); drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) of unknown frequency; occasionally rash, urticaria, itching, or purpura; rarely induction of an asthma attack, eczema, anaphylactic reactions, or photosensitivity reactions; rarely jaundice, elevated ALT, elevated AST, elevated ALP, abnormal liver function, hepatitis, or jaundice; occasionally rhinitis, bronchospasm, or acute pneumonia; rarely visual disturbances such as impaired vision and dark spots, hearing loss, tinnitus, or taste abnormality; fatigue, drowsiness, headache, or dizziness; occasionally anxiety, restlessness, confusion, or depression; rarely aseptic meningitis, severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, stiff neck, fever, or impaired consciousness; rarely mental abnormality, agitation, excitement, disorientation, or reversible toxic amblyopia; rarely lowered blood pressure, raised blood pressure, palpitations, oliguria, hematuria, proteinuria, elevated BUN and blood creatinine, hyperkalemia, decreased urine volume, generalized edema and the accompanying shortness of breath, or languor; rarely renal papillary necrosis, nephrotic syndrome, interstitial nephritis, peripheral edema, acute pulmonary edema, fluid retention, hypertension, heart failure, or reduced fertility in women; occasionally periorbital edema; very rarely malaise, fever, nosebleed, or worsening of inflammation.

Interactions

  • Do not take together with aspirin, other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, or high-dose methotrexate used in cancer chemotherapy (15 mg/week or more).
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are taking corticosteroids, alcohol, digoxin, phenytoin, probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, sulfonylureas, ACE inhibitors, angiotensin II receptor antagonists, diuretics, lithium, coumarin anticoagulants (such as warfarin), baclofen, immunosuppressants (cyclosporine, tacrolimus, sirolimus), thrombolytics, ticlopidine, antithrombotic agents, medicines that increase blood potassium levels (trimethoprim, heparin, etc.), inducers of CYP2C8 or CYP2C9 (e.g., rifampicin, phenobarbital), low-dose methotrexate (less than 15 mg/week), antiplatelet agents, or selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, if you take low-dose aspirin to prevent myocardial infarction or stroke, or if you have experienced hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to Yellow No. 5.

Those aged 15 years and over and adults take 2 capsules at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals. Those aged 8 years and over but under 15 years take 1 capsule at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.

  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after taking it 5 to 6 times, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

This medicine is used for diarrhea, for the adsorption of gas produced by abnormal fermentation in the digestive tract, and as an adsorbent for emergency detoxification in poisoning by drugs and chemicals. (However, medicinal charcoal does not adsorb cyanide, and it is relatively ineffective at adsorbing alcohol, aliphatic hydrocarbons, lithium salts, corrosive sodium chloride, heavy metals such as iron, lead, and lead cyanide, boric acid, other inorganic acids, and petroleum distillates.)

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for diarrhea, for the adsorption of gas produced by abnormal fermentation in the digestive tract,

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202302822. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Take 2 to 20 g of medicinal charcoal a day, divided into several doses. In acute poisoning, medicinal charcoal is administered within 30 minutes after ingestion of the poisonous substance. (When the amount of the ingested poisonous substance is known, the recommended dose of medicinal charcoal is usually 5-10 times the amount of the ingested poisonous substance.)
Increase or decrease the dose appropriately according to age and symptoms, following the instructions of a doctor.

Warning

  • Because it degrades the imaging of esophageal erosion, do not use it when a corrosive substance has been ingested.
  • Do not use it in patients with diabetes without a doctor's diagnosis and prescription.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine should be administered after gastric aspiration or gastric lavage has been completed with the involvement of a doctor.
  • Within 2 hours of administering medicinal charcoal, the charcoal adsorbs other medicines and so reduces their effect.
  • This medicine may turn the stools black.

Possible side effects

  • Be careful, as indigestion may occur and as the adsorption of vitamins, minerals and the like may cause nutritional disturbance.

Interactions

  • Ice cream and sherbet lower the adsorptive power of medicinal charcoal, so do not take them together with it.
  • When it is used as an antidote for oral poisoning, do not take it together with ipecac syrup.
  • The ipecac syrup may be adsorbed by the medicinal charcoal and so prevent vomiting.
  • If ipecac syrup and medicinal charcoal are used at the same time, it is recommended that the medicinal charcoal be given after vomiting has been induced and has finished.

Category

How it works

This medicine is used for rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, fever and pain due to a c

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 198601920. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

For rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, soft tissue injury, non-articular rheumatic disease, acute gout and psoriatic arthritis, adults take 200-600 mg at a time, 3-4 times a day. Up to a maximum of 3,200 mg a day may be administered. For juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, take 30-40 mg per kg of body weight at a time, 3 to 4 times a day. For mild to moderate pain and colds, adults take 200-400 mg at a time, 3 to 4 times a day. The dose may be increased or decreased as appropriate according to age and symptoms. In children, those aged 11 to 14 years take 200-250 mg (10 to 12.5 ml), those aged 7 to 10 years take 150 to 200 mg (7.5 to 10 ml), those aged 3 to 6 years take 100 to 150 mg (5 to 7.5 ml), and those aged 1 to 2 years take 50 to 100 mg (2.5 to 5 ml) at a time, 3 to 4 times a day.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic reactions, myocardial infarction and stroke, which may be fatal, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulcer and perforation may appear.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, gastrointestinal ulcers, gastrointestinal bleeding or a history of it, severe blood abnormalities, liver disorder, kidney disorder, cardiac insufficiency, high blood pressure, or bronchial asthma or a history of it, people who have experienced asthma, urticaria, or allergic reactions to aspirin or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics (including COX-2 inhibitors), patients with pain occurring before or after coronary artery (heart artery) bypass surgery (CABG), pregnant women in the last 3 months of pregnancy, patients receiving high-dose methotrexate as chemotherapy, and patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, patients with blood abnormalities or a history of them, a bleeding tendency, cirrhosis, liver disorder or a history of it, kidney disorder or a history of it, cardiac insufficiency or heart disease, high blood pressure, or a history of hypersensitivity, patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and patients with mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD), patients with ulcerative colitis, Crohn's disease, or chickenpox, elderly people, children under 2 years of age, pregnant women, and breastfeeding women should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the specified dosage and administration carefully.
  • Take care when driving or operating machinery after taking it.
  • Without the direction of a doctor or pharmacist, do not take it for pain for more than 10 days (adults) or more than 5 days (children), and do not take it for fever for more than 3 days.

Possible side effects

  • If the following occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist: shock symptoms (difficulty breathing, drop in blood pressure, etc.); blood disorders such as decreased hematocrit and hemoglobin, anemia, aplastic anemia, hemolytic anemia, agranulocytosis, decreased granulocytes, white blood cells, and platelets, reduced platelet function, and increased eosinophils; peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation (a hole), ulcerative colitis, bloody stools, gastritis, pancreatitis, vomiting of blood, Crohn's disease, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhea, stomach discomfort, upper abdominal pain, thirst, stomatitis, abdominal bloating, mouth ulcers, constipation, black stools; Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), photosensitivity reactions of unknown frequency, drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms of unknown frequency, angioneurotic edema, bullous dermatitis, erythema multiforme, maculopapular rash, reddening of the skin, blisters, rash, acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis; hepatitis, jaundice, elevated GOT, GPT, and alkaline phosphatase (ALP), liver disorder; hypersensitivity or anaphylactic reactions, asthma attacks, urticaria, eczema, purple spots, rash, itching, asthma, bronchoconstriction, difficulty breathing or wheezing; visual disturbances such as scotoma; hearing loss (deafness), tinnitus (ringing in the ears), taste disturbance, vertigo, drowsiness, dizziness, depression, headache, cerebrovascular accident or nervousness, aseptic meningitis or meningitis; drop in blood pressure, rise in blood pressure, palpitations, heart failure, myocardial infarction or angina, Kounis syndrome; acute renal failure, oliguria (decreased urination), hematuria, proteinuria, elevated BUN and blood creatinine, hyperkalemia, interstitial nephritis (kidney inflammation), nephrotic syndrome, renal papillary necrosis, decreased urine volume, generalized edema and the accompanying shortness of breath, lethargy, periorbital edema (swelling around the eyes), facial edema (facial swelling), malaise, fever, nosebleed, edema, peripheral edema, and Kounis syndrome of unknown frequency.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, alcohol or high-dose methotrexate.
  • If you take it together with ACE inhibitors, lithium, furosemide and thiazide diuretics, low-dose methotrexate, coumarin anticoagulants (warfarin, etc.), selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors or the like, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

How it works

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Children aged 12 years and under take the recommended single dose for their age group and body weight every 4 to 6 hours as needed. Refer to the approved labeling for the recommended single dose by age group and body weight. It should be taken at the lowest effective dose for the shortest possible period. Do not take more than 5 doses a day (75 mg/kg). If the body weight is known, it is more appropriate to take a dose based on body weight (10 to 15 mg/kg).

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.

  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take this medicine together with other products containing acetaminophen.

Precautions for use

  • Patients hypersensitive to this medicine, patients with peptic ulcer, severe blood abnormalities, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, or severe cardiac dysfunction, and patients with or with a history of aspirin-induced asthma (asthma attacks induced by non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs) must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, patients with or with a history of liver impairment, patients with or with a history of kidney impairment, people who have had peptic ulcer, patients with or with a history of blood abnormalities, patients with a tendency to bleed (platelet function abnormalities may occur), patients with cardiac dysfunction, people who have experienced hypersensitivity, patients with bronchial asthma, elderly people, children under 2 years of age, and pregnant or breastfeeding women should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Without the instruction of a doctor or pharmacist, do not take it for pain for more than 10 days (adults) or more than 5 days (children), and do not take it for fever for more than 3 days.
  • If pain or fever persists or worsens, or if new symptoms appear, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • If shock symptoms (difficulty breathing, reddening of the whole body, angioedema, urticaria, etc.), asthma attacks, thrombocytopenia, granulocytopenia, hemolytic (red blood cell destroying) anemia, methemoglobinemia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), cyanosis, hypersensitivity symptoms (facial swelling, difficulty breathing, sweating, low blood pressure, shock), nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, gastrointestinal bleeding with long-term use, peptic ulcer, perforation (a hole forming), rash, allergic reactions, mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), elevated AST, elevated ALT, or fixed drug eruption occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with other anti-inflammatory analgesics, other products containing acetaminophen, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, or alcohol.
  • Before taking this medicine, patients who take warfarin long term or who take lithium or thiazide diuretics should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for chronic constipation, constipation in infants, young children, and children, and constipation

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201211097. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

For chronic constipation, take this medicine before breakfast. Adults usually take 15 to 30 mL a day before breakfast for the first 2 to 3 days, and then continue with 10 to 15 mL a day. In severe cases, up to 45 mL may be given. Children aged 7 to 14 years take 15 mL a day for the first 2 to 3 days, and then continue with 10 mL a day. Young children aged 1 to 6 years take 5 to 10 mL a day. Infants under 12 months of age take 5 mL a day.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, inflammatory bowel disease (ulcerative colitis, Crohn's disease), gastrointestinal obstruction, abdominal pain of unknown cause, or a low-galactose diet (galactosemia), patients with gastrointestinal perforation or a risk of it, and patients with genetic problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and nursing mothers, infants, young children and children, elderly people, and patients with diabetes, fructose intolerance, fluid and electrolyte imbalance, acute gastritis, or chronic constipation should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after taking it for about 1 week, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If you think there has been a sudden change in your bowel habits, consult a doctor.

Possible side effects

  • If loose stools or diarrhea, rash, itching, urticaria, or erythema occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Belching, cramping abdominal discomfort, and occasionally rumbling in the abdomen, abdominal bloating, abdominal pain, loss of appetite, nausea, and vomiting may occur.

Interactions

  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking it together with glycosidase inhibitors such as acarbose, broad-spectrum antibacterial antibiotics, diuretics, corticoids, amphotericin B, cardiac glycosides, or antacids.

This medicine is used to inhibit thrombus formation in myocardial infarction, cerebral infarction, and unstable angina, to inhibit thrombus formation after coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG) or percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty (PTCA), and to reduce cardiovascular risk in high-risk patients (patients with multiple risk factors such as a family history of ischemic heart disease, high blood pressure, high cholesterol, obesity, and diabetes).

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used to inhibit thrombus formation in myocardial infarction, cerebral infarction, and unstable angina,

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201603416. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Adults take 1 tablet as 1 dose, 1 time a day. Since this medicine is an enteric-coated tablet, it may be taken before meals with plenty of water.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine or to other salicylate preparations, analgesics, anti-inflammatory agents or antirheumatic agents, patients with peptic ulcer or aspirin-induced asthma or a history of it, patients with hemophilia, severe liver disorder, severe kidney disorder, severe cardiac insufficiency or a tendency to bleed, patients receiving concomitant methotrexate at doses of 15 mg or more per week (15 mg/week), and pregnant women in the third trimester must not take this medicine.
  • Do not take this medicine during the first and second trimesters of pregnancy unless it is absolutely necessary.
  • Before using this medicine, patients with kidney disorder, cardiovascular circulatory dysfunction (renal vascular disease, congestive heart failure, fluid depletion, major surgery, sepsis or major bleeding events, etc.), liver disorder, impaired cardiac function or bronchial asthma, patients before surgery, young children aged 3 years or under, elderly people, patients with glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency, patients with Reye's syndrome, patients aged 14 years or under with chickenpox or influenza infection, and patients with gout should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Because there is a risk of bleeding, tell your doctor that you are taking this medicine if you are going to have surgery (including dental surgery).
  • Take care not to damage the enteric coating of this medicine.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms (e.g. difficulty breathing, generalized flushing, angioedema, hives), asthma attacks, hypersensitivity (erythema, itching, nasal congestion, cardiac and respiratory disorders, and sometimes rash, swelling, hives, rhinitis-like symptoms, conjunctivitis), rarely toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), skin-mucosa-eye syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), exfoliative dermatitis, rarely aplastic anemia, anemia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), ringing in the ears, deafness, dizziness, headache, agitation, rarely liver disorder, or very rarely temporary liver damage, renal impairment, acute renal failure, hyperventilation, metabolic acidosis, an excessive drop in body temperature, collapse, or coldness of the limbs occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Loss of appetite, heartburn, stomach pain, nausea, and vomiting may occur.

Interactions

  • Other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics and salicylate preparations, and methotrexate at doses of 15 mg or more per week (15 mg/week), must not be used together with this medicine, because concomitant use may increase bleeding or reduce kidney function.
  • People taking anticoagulants, some non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics such as ibuprofen and naproxen, thrombolytics, other platelet aggregation inhibitors, hemostatics, antidiabetic agents (insulin preparations, tolbutamide, etc.), uricosuric agents (benzbromarone, probenecid), thiazide diuretics, lithium preparations, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, digoxin, systemically acting adrenocortical hormone preparations (excluding hydrocortisone used as replacement therapy for Addison's disease), angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitors, or valproic acid preparations should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not mix this medicine with alkaline preparations (for example, sodium bicarbonate, magnesium carbonate) or with preparations that easily absorb moisture.
  • Concomitant use with alcohol increases damage to the gastrointestinal mucosa, and the synergistic effect of this medicine and alcohol may prolong bleeding time.

Category

How it works

This medicine is used to relieve headache, toothache, pain after tooth extraction, sore throat, ear pain, joint pain, ne

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202107347. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Those aged 15 years and over and adults take 1 to 2 capsules at a time, 1 to 3 times a day, avoiding an empty stomach. Leave an interval of at least 4 hours between doses.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Patients with uncontrolled high blood pressure, congestive heart failure, established ischemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease, or cerebrovascular disease should avoid taking high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day), and patients with cardiovascular risk factors (high blood pressure, hyperlipidemia, diabetes, smoking, etc.) should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine if high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day) is required.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, patients with hypersensitivity to soybeans or peanuts, people who have experienced allergic reactions to soybean oil, people who have had an asthma attack when taking this medicine or its ingredients, other antipyretic analgesics, or cold remedies, infants under 3 months of age, and women after 30 weeks of pregnancy must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist in the following cases: patients with hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 4 or Yellow No. 5; people who have had allergies caused by medicines (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.); infants and young children 3 months of age and older but under 2 years of age; infants and children under 15 years of age who are infected with or suspected of having chickenpox or influenza; people with liver, kidney, or thyroid disease, diabetes, or high blood pressure; elderly people; people who are physically weak or have a high fever; people with persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort, or stomach pain, or with ulcers or bleeding problems; women who are pregnant or may be pregnant; breastfeeding women; people who lose a lot of fluid through vomiting and diarrhea or who do not take in fluids, or who take diuretics; people who take low-dose aspirin to prevent myocardial infarction or stroke; patients with disorders of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinemia, diabetic hyperlipidemia, and pancreatitis, or patients who must be given lipid emulsions with caution; and patients for whom a particular risk from fat overload is expected.
  • If symptoms do not improve after taking it 5 to 6 times, consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the specified dosage and administration carefully.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking it.
  • Do not take it continuously for a long period.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness (turning red from congestion), itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, stomach pain, gastrointestinal bleeding, stomach discomfort, dizziness, edema (swelling), rarely anaphylactic shock (hypersensitivity shock: urticaria, swelling, and chest tightness immediately after taking the medicine, along with a pale complexion, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing), mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome: accompanied by high fever, with severe symptoms such as rash and redness (turning red from congestion) and blistering like burns), asthma, very rarely erythema multiforme, exfoliative dermatitis, photosensitivity reactions of unknown frequency, drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome), or acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with other antipyretic analgesics, cold medicines, or sedatives.

Why this one

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

People aged 15 years and over and adults take 1 tablet per dose, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after a meal.

Warning

  • If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported.
  • If a skin rash or another sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of 4,000 mg of acetaminophen.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine or a history of it, people who have experienced asthma when taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic or cold remedy, patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption, and infants under 3 months of age must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are an infant or a child under 15 years of age who is infected with or suspected of having chickenpox or influenza, have an allergic constitution, have experienced allergic symptoms such as fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, or itching caused by a medicine, have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, or a gastroduodenal ulcer, are physically weak or have a high fever, have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort, or stomach pain, or have ulcer or bleeding problems, are pregnant or may be pregnant, are breastfeeding, or are a child under 2 years of age.
  • If your symptoms do not improve after taking it 5 to 6 times, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the specified dosage and administration.

  • If rash, redness with congestion, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, or dizziness occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If, rarely, shock symptoms occur in which urticaria, oedema, or chest tightness appear right after taking it together with a pale complexion, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, or difficulty breathing, or if Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis, asthma, generalised listlessness, liver dysfunction such as jaundice, or interstitial pneumonia in which a cough, breathlessness, difficulty breathing, or fever may appear occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • While taking this medicine, do not take antitussives and expectorants, other cold remedies, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines.
  • Patients who are taking MAO inhibitors used for the treatment of depression or Parkinson's disease, or who are within 2 weeks of stopping them, must not take it.
  • Before taking this medicine, people who are receiving medicines for diabetes, gout, or arthritis, anticoagulants, or steroids should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Patients who have been given barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, or alcohol should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

For children aged 12 years or younger, take the recommended dose 1 time every 4 to 6 hours as needed. Refer to the approved labelling for the recommended doses by age group.

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious and potentially fatal skin reactions such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, and toxic epidermal necrolysis have been reported; if a skin rash or other signs of a hypersensitivity reaction appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, patients with peptic ulcer, severe blood abnormalities, severe liver disorder, severe kidney disorder, severe reduced cardiac function, or aspirin asthma (an asthma attack induced by non-steroidal anti-inflammatory agents), or those with a history of these, must not take this medicine.

  • Do not take this medicine together with barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, warfarin, lithium, thiazide diuretics, or other anti-inflammatory analgesics.

Category

How it works

This medicine is used for constipation.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202300044. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Adults and children aged 8 years and over take 20 to 40 mL (1 to 2 sachets) a day, based on a package unit of 1 sachet (20 mL). Depending on the symptoms, children in particular may take 20 mL (1 sachet) every two days. Dissolve 20 mL (1 sachet) of this medicine in water to make 50 mL and take it. It is recommended to take it in the morning. Children from 6 months to 7 years of age, based on a package unit of 1 sachet (8 mL), take 8 mL (1 sachet) a day at 6 months to 1 year of age, 8 to 16 mL (1 to 2 sachets) a day at 1 to 4 years of age, and 16 to 32 mL (2 to 4 sachets) a day at 4 to 7 years of age. When 1 sachet (8 mL) a day is taken, take it in the morning, and when more than 1 sachet (8 mL) a day is taken, divide it between morning and evening. Dissolve 8 mL (1 sachet) of this medicine in water to make 50 mL and take it.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be taken by patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, by patients with inflammatory bowel disease (ulcerative colitis, Crohn's disease, etc.) or toxic megacolon, by patients with intestinal perforation or at risk of intestinal perforation, by patients who have or are suspected of having intestinal obstruction, by patients with intestinal stricture, or by patients with abdominal pain of unknown cause.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant or a breast-feeding woman, has acute constipation that is not caused by a change in lifestyle habits or acute constipation accompanied by pain, fever or abdominal distension, has irritable bowel syndrome, or has a hypersensitivity reaction to macrogol (polyethylene glycol).
  • In children, do not give this medicine for 3 months or more, and do not give this medicine for a long period without the judgment of a doctor.

Possible side effects

  • In adults, if abdominal pain and abdominal distension, diarrhea or nausea appears, if vomiting, urgent defecation or fecal incontinence uncommonly appears, if electrolyte disturbance (hyponatremia, hypokalemia, etc.), dehydration or erythema appears at an unknown frequency, or if a hypersensitivity reaction (itching, rash, facial edema, angioedema, urticaria, anaphylactic shock, etc.) very rarely appears, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • In children, if abdominal pain, diarrhea or perianal pain caused by diarrhea appears, if vomiting, abdominal distension or nausea uncommonly appears, or if a hypersensitivity reaction (hypersensitivity, angioedema, urticaria, rash, itching, etc.) appears at an unknown frequency, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Those aged 15 years and over take 24 mL (2 sachets) at a time, those aged 11 years and over but under 15 years take 16 mL (1 and 1/3 sachets) at a time, those aged 7 years and over but under 11 years take 12 mL (1 sachet) at a time, those aged 3 years and over but under 7 years take 8 mL (2/3 sachet) at a time, and those aged 2 years and over but under 3 years take 6 mL (1/2 sachet) at a time, three times a day, 30 minutes after meals.   • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.

  • Those with hypersensitivity to this medicine or who have experienced it, those who have experienced asthma when taking other antipyretic analgesics or cold remedies, infants under 3 months of age, breastfeeding women, and people who are taking MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.) or who stopped taking them within the past 2 weeks must not take this medicine.Before taking this medicine, infants infected with or suspected of having chickenpox or influenza and children under 15 years of age, infants and young children aged 3 months and older but under 2 years, those with an allergic constitution, those who have experienced allergic symptoms (e.g. fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.), those with liver, kidney, heart, or thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, edema, or gastroduodenal ulcer, elderly people, physically weak people or people with a high fever, people with persistent or recurring gastrointestinal problems such as heartburn, gastric discomfort, or stomach pain or with ulcer or bleeding problems, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant, and people who smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough persisting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever and rash or persistent headache should consult a doctor or pharmacist.Strictly observe the specified dosage and administration.When administering to children, do so under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.Do not take it continuously over a long period.Do not drink alcohol while taking it.Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.If there is no improvement in symptoms after taking it about 5 to 6 times, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with other products containing acetaminophen, MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinson drugs, etc.), antitussives (which stop coughing) and expectorants (phlegm medicines), other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis, motion sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines).

This medicine is used for diarrhea, for the adsorption of gas produced by abnormal fermentation in the digestive tract, and as an adsorbent for emergency detoxification in cases of poisoning by medicines and chemicals.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for diarrhea, for the adsorption of gas produced by abnormal fermentation in the digestive tract,

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202302823. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Take 2 to 20 g of medicinal charcoal in 1 day, divided into several doses. In acute poisoning, administer medicinal charcoal within 30 minutes after ingestion of the poisonous substance. When the amount of poisonous substance ingested is known, the recommended dose of medicinal charcoal is usually 5-10 times the amount of the ingested poisonous substance. Increase or decrease the amount appropriately according to age and symptoms as directed by a doctor.

Warning

  • Since this medicine impairs the imaging of esophageal erosion, do not take it if a corrosive substance has been ingested.
  • Do not use this medicine in patients with diabetes without a doctor's diagnosis and prescription.

Precautions for use

  • When this medicine is used as an antidote for oral poisoning, giving medicinal charcoal together with ipecac syrup is not recommended, because the ipecac syrup is adsorbed by the medicinal charcoal and vomiting is thereby prevented.
  • If ipecac syrup and medicinal charcoal are used together, it is recommended that the medicinal charcoal be given after vomiting has been induced and completed.
  • This medicine should be given after gastric aspiration or gastric lavage has been completed with the involvement of a doctor.
  • Within 2 hours of giving medicinal charcoal, the charcoal adsorbs other medicines and therefore reduces their effect.
  • This medicine may colour the stool black.

Possible side effects

  • Indigestion may occur.

Interactions

  • Ice cream and sherbet lower the adsorptive power of medicinal charcoal, so do not take them together with this medicine.

Adults take 1 bottle (50 mL) at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.

  • Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine and those who have experienced it, those who have experienced asthma when taking other antipyretic analgesics or cold remedies, children under 2 years of age, and people who are taking MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.) or who stopped taking them within the past 2 weeks must not take this medicine.Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist in the case of infants infected with or suspected of having chickenpox or influenza and children under 15 years of age, those with an allergic constitution, those who have experienced allergic symptoms caused by medicines, people with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma, or difficulty urinating, elderly people, physically weak people or people with a high fever, people with persistent or recurring gastrointestinal problems such as heartburn, gastric discomfort, or stomach pain or with ulcer or bleeding problems, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women, and people who smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough persisting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever and rash or persistent headache.Strictly observe the specified dosage and administration.If there is no improvement in symptoms after taking it 5 to 6 times, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with antitussive (cough-stopping) expectorants (phlegm remedies), other cold remedies, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis (nasal inflammation), motion sickness remedies, allergy remedies).

This medicine is used to inhibit thrombus formation in myocardial infarction, cerebral infarction, and unstable angina, to inhibit thrombus formation after coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG) or percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty (PTCA), and to reduce cardiovascular risk in high-risk patients (patients with multiple risk factors such as a family history of ischemic heart disease, high blood pressure, high cholesterol, obesity, and diabetes).

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used to inhibit thrombus formation in myocardial infarction, cerebral infarction, and unstable angina,

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201310592. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Adults take 1 tablet as 1 dose, 1 time a day. Since this medicine is an enteric-coated tablet, it may be taken before meals with plenty of water.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine or to other salicylate preparations, analgesics, anti-inflammatory agents or antirheumatic agents, patients with peptic ulcer or aspirin-induced asthma or a history of it, patients with hemophilia, severe liver disorder, severe kidney disorder, severe cardiac insufficiency or a tendency to bleed, patients receiving concomitant methotrexate at doses of 15 mg or more per week (15 mg/week), and pregnant women in the third trimester must not take this medicine.
  • Do not take this medicine during the first and second trimesters of pregnancy unless it is absolutely necessary.
  • Before using this medicine, patients with kidney disorder, cardiovascular circulatory dysfunction (renal vascular disease, congestive heart failure, fluid depletion, major surgery, sepsis or major bleeding events, etc.), liver disorder, impaired cardiac function or bronchial asthma, patients before surgery, young children aged 3 years or under, elderly people, patients with glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency, patients with Reye's syndrome, patients aged 14 years or under with chickenpox or influenza infection, and patients with gout should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Because there is a risk of bleeding, tell your doctor that you are taking this medicine if you are going to have surgery (including dental surgery).
  • Take care not to damage the enteric coating of this medicine.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms (e.g., difficulty breathing, generalized flushing, angioedema, urticaria), asthma attacks, hypersensitivity (erythema, itching, nasal congestion, cardiac and respiratory disorders, occasionally rash, edema, urticaria, rhinitis-like symptoms, conjunctivitis), rarely toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), exfoliative dermatitis, aplastic anemia, anemia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), ringing in the ears, deafness, dizziness, headache, agitation, liver disorder, very rarely transient liver damage, kidney disorder, acute renal failure, hyperventilation, metabolic acidosis, excessive lowering of body temperature, collapse, or coldness of the limbs occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Loss of appetite, heartburn, stomach pain, nausea, and vomiting may occur.

Interactions

  • Other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics and salicylate preparations, and methotrexate at doses of 15 mg or more per week (15 mg/week), must not be used together with this medicine, because concomitant use may increase bleeding or reduce kidney function.
  • People taking anticoagulants, some non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics such as ibuprofen and naproxen, thrombolytics, other platelet aggregation inhibitors, hemostatics, antidiabetic agents (insulin preparations, tolbutamide, etc.), uricosuric agents (benzbromarone, probenecid), thiazide diuretics, lithium preparations, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, digoxin, systemically acting adrenocortical hormone preparations (excluding hydrocortisone used as replacement therapy for Addison's disease), angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitors, or valproic acid preparations should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not mix this medicine with alkaline preparations (for example, sodium bicarbonate, magnesium carbonate) or with preparations that easily absorb moisture.
  • Concomitant use with alcohol increases damage to the gastrointestinal mucosa, and the synergistic effect of this medicine and alcohol may prolong bleeding time.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Children aged 6 to 12 years take 1 dose of 10 mL every 4 to 6 hours, and children aged 2 to 6 years take 5 mL every 4 to 6 hours. Do not take 4 or more doses within 24 hours.

Warning

  • If a severe skin adverse reaction such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis appears, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is a child under 2 years of age; if you have an allergic constitution or have experienced allergic reactions (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.); if you have a disease such as liver impairment, renal impairment (kidney disorder), thyroid disease, or diabetes; if you have a high fever or are frail; if you have diabetes or another such condition; if you are frail or have a high fever; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant, or are breastfeeding; if you have heart disease or high blood pressure; or if you have a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm or a persistent or chronic cough such as asthma.
  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after taking it several times, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If a cough lasts for 7 days or more or is accompanied by fever or a persistent headache, consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • When giving it to a child, administer it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Possible side effects

  • If rash, redness (congested and reddened), nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, dizziness, anxiety, insomnia, or severe skin adverse reactions such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, fever, erythema (red spots), or numerous small pustules occur, if a cough lasts for 7 days or more or is accompanied by fever or a persistent headache, or if ischemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding, etc.) occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If symptoms of reversible posterior encephalopathy syndrome or reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizures, visual disturbance, etc.) occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with MAO inhibitors, other antitussive (cough-stopping) expectorants (cold remedies), cold remedies, antihistamines, sedatives, or alcohol.
  • People within 2 weeks of stopping MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.) must not take this medicine.

  • If, rarely, nausea, vomiting, stomatitis, heartburn, diarrhea, urticaria, itching, rash, headache, tinnitus, bronchospasm (especially in asthma patients), tachycardia, hypertension, and very rarely anaphylaxis or the like appear, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Why this one
