  • If rash and redness (congested and reddened skin), itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema (swelling), difficulty urinating, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, rarely shock (urticaria, edema (swelling) and chest tightness together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing, etc.), Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome) (when severe symptoms accompanied by high fever, with rash and redness (congested and reddened skin) and blistering like a burn, appear on the skin all over the body and on the mucous membranes of the mouth or eyes), asthma, liver function disorder (generalized listlessness, jaundice (the skin or the whites of the eyes turning yellow), etc.), interstitial pneumonia (accompanied by coughing, breathlessness, difficulty breathing, fever, etc.), symptoms of ischemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding, etc.), or posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome and reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizure, visual disturbance, etc.) occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic reactions, myocardial infarction and stroke, which may be fatal, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulcer and perforation may appear.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be taken by patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, peptic ulcer, severe blood abnormality, liver impairment, renal impairment, cardiac insufficiency, high blood pressure or bronchial asthma or by those who have had them, by people who have had asthma, urticaria or an allergy in response to aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic, by patients being treated for pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass surgery, or by a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant or a breast-feeding woman.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user has or has had peptic ulcer, blood abnormality, a bleeding tendency, liver impairment, renal impairment, cardiac insufficiency, high blood pressure or hypersensitivity, is a patient with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) or mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD), ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease, is elderly or a child, has stomach cancer, or is taking low-dose aspirin to prevent myocardial infarction or stroke, especially a patient with an autoimmune disease (SLE, MCTD).

  • If any of the following appears, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist: rarely shock (chest discomfort, chills, difficulty breathing, fall in blood pressure, etc.); blood disorders such as aplastic anemia, hemolytic anemia, granulocytopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time) and eosinophilia; peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stools, gastritis, pancreatitis, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhea, stomach discomfort, or very rarely dry mouth, stomatitis, abdominal distension and constipation; Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) or toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome); drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) of unknown frequency; acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis; jaundice and increases in GOT, GPT and AL-P; induction of an asthma attack; urticaria, eczema, purpura, occasionally rash and itching; rarely visual disturbance such as blurred or dim vision, hearing loss, tinnitus and abnormal taste; aseptic meningitis, severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, a stiff neck, fever or disturbance of consciousness; fall in blood pressure, rise in blood pressure and palpitations; acute renal failure, oliguria and hematuria together with proteinuria and increases in BUN and blood creatinine; hyperkalemia, reduced urine volume, generalized edema and the accompanying shortness of breath and languor; acute pulmonary edema; occasionally periorbital edema; and very rarely malaise, fever and nosebleed.

Interactions

  • Do not use it together with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when using it together with glucocorticoids, alcohol, digoxin, phenytoin, probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, sulfonylureas, diuretics, antihypertensive medicines, ACE inhibitors, furosemide, aspirin, lithium, methotrexate, or coumarin anticoagulants (such as warfarin).

  • Patients who are hypersensitive to this medicine or have experienced such hypersensitivity, people who have experienced asthma when taking other antipyretic analgesics or cold medicines, infants under 3 months of age, and patients with severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure must not take this medicine.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202303193. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Adults take 20 ml as 1 dose, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause liver damage.

  • Do not take more than the maximum daily amount of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine or those who have experienced it, people who have experienced asthma when taking this medicine or its ingredients, other antipyretic analgesics, or cold remedies, and infants under 3 months of age and children under 2 years of age should not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, people with an allergic constitution, people who have experienced allergic symptoms from medicines such as fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, or itching, infants and children under 15 years of age who are infected with or suspected of having chickenpox or influenza, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant, breastfeeding women, children under 2 years of age when use is unavoidable, people who are physically weak or have a high fever, people with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma, or difficulty urinating, people whose gastrointestinal problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort, or stomach pain persist or recur or who have ulcers or bleeding problems, and people with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, or emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts 1 week or more or recurs, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash, or persistent headache should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Children should take it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Do not take it continuously for a long period.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration exactly.

  • If rash and redness, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema, difficulty urinating, (persistent or severe) thirst, or dizziness occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Rarely, if shock (anaphylaxis), in which urticaria, swelling, and chest tightness appear right after taking the medicine together with a pale complexion, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing, or mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), asthma, general languor, liver dysfunction such as jaundice, or interstitial pneumonia occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • While taking this medicine, do not take antitussive expectorants, other cold remedies, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines.

Category

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202301170. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Adults and those 12 years and older take 2 tablets at a time, twice a day, and those 36 months and older but under 12 years take 1 tablet at a time, twice a day, dissolving it in the mouth or chewing it after meals.

Warning

  • Taking 5,000 IU or more of vitamin A a day may cause congenital malformations.
  • Women within 3 months of pregnancy or women who may be pregnant must not take it.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypercalcemia (a condition in which there is an excess of calcium in the blood), sarcoidosis (a systemic inflammatory disease of unknown cause), kidney disease or hypersensitivity to this medicine, nursing infants under 12 months of age, patients with kidney stones or severe renal failure, and patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption must not take this medicine.

  • If nausea, vomiting, itching, dry and rough skin, painful joint swelling, diarrhea, gastric discomfort, constipation, rash, redness, loose stools, hypotension, facial flushing, irregular heartbeat, skin rash, red spots, asystole (cardiac arrest), depression of central nervous system function, gastrointestinal disorders, digestive disturbance, upper abdominal pain, pulmonary edema, or symptoms such as menstruation starting earlier than expected, becoming progressively heavier, or bleeding lasting a long time occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids, or levodopa.
  • If you take it together with oral contraceptives containing estrogen, consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Because concomitant use with antialdosterone agents or triamterene may cause hyperkalemia, consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Avoid teas containing tannin such as green tea and black tea while taking it and just before and after taking it.

For rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, soft tissue injury, non-articular rheumatic disease, acute gout and psoriatic arthritis, adults take 200-600 mg at a time, 3-4 times a day. Up to a maximum of 3,200 mg a day may be administered. For juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, take 30-40 mg per kg of body weight at a time, 3 to 4 times a day. For mild to moderate pain and colds, adults take 200-400 mg at a time, 3 to 4 times a day. The dose may be increased or decreased as appropriate according to age and symptoms. In children, those aged 11 to 14 years take 200-250 mg (10 to 12.5 ml), those aged 7 to 10 years take 150 to 200 mg (7.5 to 10 ml), those aged 3 to 6 years take 100 to 150 mg (5 to 7.5 ml), and those aged 1 to 2 years take 50 to 100 mg (2.5 to 5 ml) at a time, 3 to 4 times a day.

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

Adults and children aged 8 years and older take 20 to 40 ml (1 to 2 packets) a day, based on a package unit of 1 packet (20 ml). Depending on symptoms, children in particular may take 20 ml (1 packet) every other day. Dissolve 20 ml (1 packet) of this medicine in water to make 50 ml and then take it. It is recommended to take it in the morning. For children from 6 months to 7 years of age, based on a package unit of 1 packet (8 ml), children 6 months to 1 year of age take 8 ml (1 packet) a day, children 1 to 4 years of age take 8 to 16 ml (1 to 2 packets) a day, and children 4 to 7 years of age take 16 to 32 ml (2 to 4 packets) a day. If 1 packet (8 ml) a day is taken, take it in the morning; if more than 1 packet (8 ml) a day is taken, divide the dose between morning and evening. Dissolve 8 ml (1 packet) of this medicine in water to make 50 ml and then take it.

  • People who are hypersensitive to this medicine and patients with inflammatory bowel disease (ulcerative colitis, Crohn's disease, etc.), toxic megacolon, intestinal perforation, intestinal obstruction, intestinal stricture, or abdominal pain of unknown cause must not take this medicine.
  • Do not take this medicine for a long period without a doctor's judgment.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant, or are breastfeeding, if you have acute constipation not caused by a change in lifestyle habits (such as acute constipation accompanied by pain, fever, or abdominal distension), if you have irritable bowel syndrome, or if you have a hypersensitivity reaction to macrogol (polyethylene glycol).
  • Do not give this medicine to children for more than 3 months.

  • In adults, if abdominal pain and bloating, diarrhea, or nausea occurs, uncommonly vomiting or urgent bowel movements, with unknown frequency fecal incontinence, electrolyte disturbances (hyponatremia, hypokalemia, etc.), dehydration, or erythema, or very rarely hypersensitivity reactions (itching, rash, facial swelling, angioedema, hives, anaphylaxis, shock, etc.), stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Category

How it works

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Adults take 1 capsule per dose, 1 time a day. Since this medicine is an enteric-coated capsule, it may be taken before meals with plenty of water.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine or other salicylate preparations, patients with peptic ulcer, patients with aspirin-induced asthma (induction of asthma attacks by non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, etc.) or those who have experienced it, patients with hemophilia, severe hepatic impairment, severe renal impairment, cardiac insufficiency, or a bleeding tendency, patients receiving concomitant methotrexate at a dose of 15 milligrams or more per week (15 mg/week), and pregnant women in the third trimester of pregnancy should not take this medicine.

  • Take care not to damage the enteric coating of this medicine.
  • If you are to undergo surgery (including dental surgery), you must tell the doctor in charge that you are taking an aspirin preparation and receive advice.

  • If shock symptoms (for example, difficulty breathing, generalized flushing, angioedema, urticaria), asthma attacks, erythema, itching, nasal congestion, cardiac and respiratory disorders, occasionally rash, swelling, urticaria, rhinitis symptoms, conjunctivitis, rarely toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), exfoliative dermatitis, rarely aplastic anemia, anemia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), ringing in the ears, hearing loss, dizziness, headache, agitation, rarely liver disorder, very rarely temporary liver damage with elevated liver transaminases, kidney disorder, acute renal failure, hyperventilation, metabolic acidosis, excessive drop in body temperature, collapse, or coldness of the limbs occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Loss of appetite, heartburn, stomach pain, nausea, and vomiting may occur.

  • Do not use it together with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, salicylate preparations, or high-dose methotrexate.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking it together with anticoagulants, thrombolytics or other platelet aggregation inhibitors, hemostatics, antidiabetic medicines (insulin preparations, tolbutamide, etc.), uricosuric agents (benzbromarone, probenecid), lithium preparations, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, digoxin, systemically acting adrenocortical hormone preparations (except hydrocortisone used as replacement therapy for Addison's disease), angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors, valproic acid, or alkaline preparations (e.g. sodium bicarbonate, magnesium carbonate).
  • When taken together with alcohol, damage to the gastrointestinal mucosa may increase and bleeding time may be prolonged.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used to relieve the various symptoms of a cold, such as sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills with shiveri

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202303363. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Those aged 15 years and over take 1 sachet (20 mL) at a time, those aged 11 years and over but under 15 years take 2/3 of a sachet at a time, those aged 7 years and over but under 11 years take 1/2 of a sachet, those aged 3 years and over but under 7 years take 1/3 of a sachet at a time, and those aged 2 years and over but under 3 years take 1/4 of a sachet, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals. Allow an interval of 4 hours between doses.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), have been reported, and if a skin rash or another sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily amount of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine or those who have experienced it, those who have experienced asthma when taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics or cold remedies, infants under 3 months of age, and children under 2 years of age must not take this medicine.Before taking this medicine, children under 2 years of age in cases where it is strictly necessary, infants infected with or suspected of having chickenpox or influenza and children under 15 years of age, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant, breastfeeding women, elderly people, and physically weak people or people with a high fever should consult a doctor or pharmacist.Before taking this medicine, those with an allergic constitution, those who have experienced allergic symptoms caused by medicines such as fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, or itching, people with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, or gastroduodenal ulcer, people with persistent or recurring gastrointestinal problems such as heartburn, gastric discomfort, or stomach pain or with ulcer or bleeding problems, and people who smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough persisting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever and rash or persistent headache should consult a doctor or pharmacist.If symptoms do not improve after taking it 5 to 6 times, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.Children should take it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.Do not take it continuously over a long period.Strictly observe the specified dosage and administration.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, dizziness, edema, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, or insomnia occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If, rarely, shock (anaphylaxis) occurs — in which urticaria, edema, and chest tightness appear right after taking it, together with a pale complexion, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing — or if Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), asthma, general lethargy, liver function disorders such as jaundice, or interstitial pneumonia occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • While taking this medicine, do not take antitussives and expectorants, other cold remedies, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines.
  • People who are taking an MAO inhibitor used for depression, Parkinson's disease, and the like, or who stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks, should not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, people who are receiving diabetes medicines, gout medicines, arthritis medicines, anticoagulants, or steroids should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Patients who have taken barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, or alcohol should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not drink alcohol when taking it.

This medicine is used for rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis (degenerative joint disease), fever and pain due to a cold, low back pain, dysmenorrhea, post-operative pain and ankylosing spondylitis, headache, toothache, muscle pain, neuralgia, acute gout, psoriatic arthritis, soft tissue injury (sprain, contusion), and non-articular rheumatic diseases (tendinitis, tenosynovitis, bursitis).

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis (degenerative joint diseas

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 199804309. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

For rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, soft tissue injury, non-articular rheumatic disease, acute gout and psoriatic arthritis, adults take 1/2 tablet to 1.5 tablets (200 to 600 mg) per dose 3 to 4 times a day, up to a maximum of 3200 mg a day. For juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, take 30 to 40 mg per kg of body weight a day, divided into 3 to 4 doses; for mild to moderate pain or a cold, adults take 1/2 tablet to 1 tablet (200 to 400 mg) per dose 3 to 4 times a day. Children aged 11 to 14 years take 200 to 250 mg per dose, children aged 7 to 10 years take 150 to 200 mg per dose, children aged 3 to 6 years take 100 to 150 mg per dose, and children aged 1 to 2 years take 50 to 100 mg per dose, orally 3 to 4 times a day. For children weighing less than 30 kg the daily amount must not exceed 500 mg, and it is preferable to avoid taking it on an empty stomach. Do not take more than the recommended amount.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic reactions, myocardial infarction and stroke, which may be fatal, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulcer and perforation may appear.
  • Patients with uncontrolled high blood pressure, congestive heart failure, established ischemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease or cerebrovascular disease must avoid taking high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day), and patients who have cardiovascular risk factors (high blood pressure, hyperlipidemia, diabetes, smoking, etc.) and need to take high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day) should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be taken by patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, by patients who have or have had gastrointestinal ulcer or gastrointestinal bleeding, by patients with severe blood abnormality, severe liver impairment, severe renal impairment, severe cardiac insufficiency or severe high blood pressure, by patients who have or have had bronchial asthma, by patients who have or have had hypersensitivity such as asthma, urticaria or an allergic reaction to aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic (including COX-2 inhibitors), by patients with pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass surgery, by pregnant women in the last 3 months of pregnancy, by patients taking high-dose methotrexate as anticancer therapy, or by patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user has or has had blood abnormality, has a bleeding tendency, has or has had cirrhosis or liver impairment, has or has had renal impairment, has cardiac insufficiency or heart disease, high blood pressure, a history of hypersensitivity, systemic lupus erythematosus or mixed connective tissue disease, ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease, is elderly or a child, is a pregnant woman or a breast-feeding woman, or is taking low-dose aspirin to prevent myocardial infarction or stroke.
  • Without the direction of a doctor or pharmacist, do not take it for pain for 10 days or more (adults) or 5 days or more (children), and do not take it for fever for 3 days or more.

Possible side effects

  • If any of the following appears, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist: symptoms of shock (heartburn, chills, difficulty breathing, fall in blood pressure); blood disorders such as decreased hematocrit, decreased hemoglobin, anemia, aplastic anemia, hemolytic anemia, agranulocytosis, granulocytopenia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time) and eosinophilia; peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stools, gastritis, pancreatitis, hematemesis, Crohn's disease, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhea, stomach discomfort, upper abdominal pain, thirst, stomatitis, abdominal distension, oral ulcer, constipation and black stools; mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), photosensitivity reaction, drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) of unknown frequency, angioneurotic edema, bullous dermatitis, erythema multiforme, maculopapular rash, reddening of the skin, blisters, rash, exfoliative dermatitis and acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis; hepatitis, jaundice, hepatic dysfunction such as increases in GOT, GPT and ALP, and liver impairment; hypersensitivity or anaphylactic reaction, asthma attack, urticaria, eczema, purpura, rash, itching, asthma, bronchoconstriction, difficulty breathing or wheezing; visual disturbance such as a blind area of the visual field, hearing loss, tinnitus and abnormal taste; vertigo, drowsiness, dizziness, depression, headache, cerebrovascular accident or nervousness; aseptic meningitis or meningitis (symptoms such as severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, a stiff neck, fever or disturbance of consciousness); rise in blood pressure, palpitations, heart failure, myocardial infarction or angina; acute renal failure, oliguria, hematuria, proteinuria, increases in BUN and blood creatinine, hyperkalemia, interstitial nephritis, nephrotic syndrome, renal papillary necrosis, reduced urine volume, generalized edema and the accompanying shortness of breath and languor; and, at an unknown frequency, Conn's syndrome, periorbital swelling, facial swelling, malaise, fever, nosebleed and peripheral edema.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, low-dose aspirin, or high-dose methotrexate.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking it together with ACE inhibitors, lithium, furosemide and thiazide diuretics, coumarin anticoagulants (such as warfarin), or selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors.

Oral medicine (MFDS 202303193)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202303193. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is used to relieve various symptoms of a cold, such as runny nose, nasal congestion, sneezing, sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills, fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used to relieve various symptoms of a cold, such as runny nose, nasal congestion, sneezing, sore throat

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202303193. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Adults take 20 ml as 1 dose, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), have been reported, and if a skin rash or another sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily amount of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine or those who have experienced it, people who have experienced asthma when taking this medicine or its ingredients, other antipyretic analgesics, or cold remedies, and infants under 3 months of age and children under 2 years of age should not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, people with an allergic constitution, people who have experienced allergic symptoms from medicines such as fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, or itching, infants and children under 15 years of age who are infected with or suspected of having chickenpox or influenza, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant, breastfeeding women, children under 2 years of age when use is unavoidable, people who are physically weak or have a high fever, people with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma, or difficulty urinating, people whose gastrointestinal problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort, or stomach pain persist or recur or who have ulcers or bleeding problems, and people with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, or emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts 1 week or more or recurs, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash, or persistent headache should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Children should take it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Do not take it continuously for a long period.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration exactly.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema, difficulty urinating, (persistent or severe) thirst, or dizziness occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Rarely, if shock (anaphylaxis), in which urticaria, swelling, and chest tightness appear right after taking the medicine together with a pale complexion, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing, or mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), asthma, general languor, liver dysfunction such as jaundice, or interstitial pneumonia occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • While taking this medicine, do not take antitussive expectorants, other cold remedies, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines.
  • People who are taking MAO inhibitors used for the treatment of depression or Parkinson's disease, or who are within 2 weeks of stopping them, must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, people who are receiving diabetes medicines, gout medicines, arthritis medicines, anticoagulants, or steroids should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Patients receiving barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, or alcohol should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.
  • This medicine contains saccharin.

payloads.content:

Oral medicine (MFDS 199700386)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 199700386. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is used for iron deficiency anemia.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for iron deficiency anemia.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 199700386. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Adults take 100 mg as iron once a day; children aged 12 years and older to under 19 years take 50 mg as iron at a time, twice a day; children aged 1 year and older to under 12 years take 50 mg as iron at a time, 1 to 2 times a day; and children aged 1 year and under take 15–50 mg as iron once a day, before, during, or after a meal.

Warning

  • An overdose in children aged 6 years or younger may cause fatal iron poisoning, so keep this medicine out of the reach of children.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, and patients with hemochromatosis (a disease in which iron is deposited in the liver and pancreas due to abnormal iron metabolism), hemosiderosis, non-iron-deficiency anemia, impaired iron utilization, iron overload, anemia due to bone marrow insufficiency, chronic hemolytic anemia, iron deficiency anemia due to infection or tumor, chronic pancreatitis, or liver cirrhosis must not take this medicine.Before taking this medicine, infants under 12 months of age, patients with gastrointestinal diseases such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis, or regional colitis, patients with cardiac and circulatory system dysfunction, paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria, kidney impairment, or hypoproteinemia, and patients receiving repeated blood transfusions should consult a doctor or pharmacist.Strictly observe the specified dosage and administration.When administering to children, do so under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Possible side effects

  • If urticaria, itching, skin hypersensitivity reactions on exposure to sunlight, abdominal or stomach pain, stomach cramps, vomiting, diarrhea, fever, coma, occasionally elevated AST and ALT, rarely elevated ALP, nausea, loss of appetite, constipation, black stools, tooth discoloration, stomach discomfort, or toxicity occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take it together with phosphates, calcium salts, parenteral iron preparations, or parenteral iron(III) hydroxide polymaltose complex preparations.If taking it together with iron-containing preparations (iron supplements, liver contrast agents for MRI, etc.), antialdosterone agents, triamterene, diphosphonate salts, thyroxine, cefdinir preparations, quinolones, penicillamine, cholestyramine, preparations such as pancreatic extract and vitamin E, or 200 mg or more of ascorbic acid (vitamin C), consult a doctor or pharmacist.Avoid teas containing tannin, such as green tea and black tea, and milk and dairy products while taking it and before and after taking it.

payloads.content:

Oral medicine (MFDS 202204271)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202204271. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is used for cough and phlegm.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for cough and phlegm.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202204271. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Those aged 15 years and older take 1 sachet (1.2 g) at a time; those aged 11 years and older but under 15 years take 2/3 sachet (0.8 g) at a time; those aged 8 years and older but under 11 years take 1/2 sachet (0.6 g) at a time; those aged 5 years and older but under 8 years take 1/3 sachet (0.4 g) at a time; those aged 3 years and older but under 5 years take 1/4 sachet (0.3 g) at a time; and those aged 2 years and older but under 3 years take 1/5 sachet (0.24 g) at a time, 3 to 4 times a day.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, infants (nursing infants, newborns) under 3 months of age, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant, and patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption must not take this medicine.Before taking this medicine, those with an allergic constitution, those who have experienced allergic reactions (fever, rash (congested and reddened skin), joint pain, itching, etc.), people with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, or edema (swelling), elderly people, physically weak people or people with a high fever, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women, people under the care of a doctor or dentist, and patients with cough (smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough persisting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, a cough accompanied by fever and rash (congested and reddened skin) or persistent headache) should consult a doctor or pharmacist.If there is no improvement in symptoms after taking it 5 to 6 times, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.When administering it to those under 2 years of age, consult a doctor or pharmacist.Strictly observe the specified dosage and administration.When using it in children, do so under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness (congested and reddened skin), itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, dizziness, rarely pseudoaldosteronism (a decrease in urine volume, swelling of the face, hands and feet, heaviness of the eyelids, stiffening of the hands, a rise in blood pressure or headache, etc.), or myopathy (weakness, cramps in the limbs, paralysis) occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.), other antitussives and expectorants, cold remedies, antihistamines, sedatives, or alcohol.
  • Do not take it together with potassium-containing preparations, licorice-containing preparations, preparations containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, loop diuretics (furosemide, ethacrynic acid), or thiazide diuretics (trichlormethiazide).

Those aged 8 years and older take 1 sachet at a time, once a day.

  • If symptoms such as nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
